### Day 58: 2 Samuel 12:1-12
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-58-2-samuel-12-1-12.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 12:9
Points:
- Nathan required courage and divine guidance to confront an autocratic king, showing that confrontation must be motivated solely by sin.
- Using a relatable parable, the prophet led David to evaluate the situation objectively before delivering God's rebuke.
- God revealed David's deep ingratitude by noting that He had provided abundantly and would have given even more.
- David pronounced his own condemnation, allowing him to realize the depth of mercy when granted an undeserved reprieve.
- The Lord forgives the repentant sinner while still maintaining judgment and discipline over the consequences of sin.

### Devotional: 2 Samuel 12
Author: D.A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-samuel-12-2-corinthians-5-ezekiel-19-psalms-64-65/
Passage: 2 Samuel 12:7
Points:
- Nathan combined moral boldness with astute storytelling to pierce King David's defenses and expose his wrongdoing.
- The crucial difference between David and Saul lies in how they received rebuke, with David responding in authentic brokenness.
- Genuine believers may fall into serious sin, but true faith is proven by sincere contrition rather than making excuses.
- While God graciously pardons sin and removes its ultimate penalty, unavoidable earthly consequences and hardships often remain.
- David understood God as a personal Lord who can be pursued in prayer rather than an unfeeling fate.
